liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Reviewer ranks it among their favorite versions, praising Jerry's fast, tasteful, sweet-toned licks [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer says this was the first-ever performance of Scarlet Begonias [14]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Reviewer says this was the first-ever performance of Cassidy [14]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Phil's series of power chords in the bridge was physically felt in the crowd, like thunder [12]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer, who attended, recalls this version exploding with more bottom end than they had heard before or since [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Part 1**: rare: 10 archived performances [22]
- **Part 1**: rare: 10 archived performances [22]
- **Playin' In The Band**: with false start [22]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Cassidy [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-03-23.sbd.matrix.tobin.82507.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 33 songs; 206 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1974-03-23.aud.connors.hughey.gems.78599.flac16**: audience recording; 32 songs; 206 min; rated 4.5/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: A whistler audible on the audience recording stops or gets covered up; Taper's sound seems to improve during the song, possibly as the band tunes up; piano solo runs hot [2][16]
- **gd1974-03-23.aud.OBV-GEMS.83453.flac16**: audience recording; 32 songs; 206 min; rated 3.6/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has little crowd noise, with clear instruments and vocals, and Keith's playing stands out; Several hundred loud handclaps were removed and most tunings were cut [3][15]
- **gd1974-03-23.176294.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 33 songs; 206 min [4]
- **gd74-03-23.sbd.clugston.1689.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 30 songs; 202 min; rated 3.89/5 by 9 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says most of the remembered bass power from the soundtest is present on this release; Jerry's guitar tone, combined with the Wall's output, sounds like ethereal bells [12][13]

## Around the show

- Guests: false start [1]
- The band badly botched the opening, played spacey stuff, then Bob apologized [17]
- Reviewer attended but was in a bad mood before entering and enjoyed it less than the recording [19]
- Reviewer attended but was in a bad mood before entering and enjoyed it less than the recording [20]
- The core of the show is on Disc 2, needing an 80-minute disc [1]
- Reviewer calls it the first show with the Wall of Sound [10]
- Described as a historic show, the first with the Wall of Sound [3]
- First show using the complete Wall Of Sound; featured on Dick's Picks 24 [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-03-23.sbd.matrix.tobin.82507.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (65%-SBD/35%-AUD) [1]. Also: Soundboard master reel went to DAT then CDR; a cassette-to-DAT source supplies the first seconds of Ship Of Fools; Audience source patches Morning Dew and Sugar Magnolia; Scott Clugston did EAC to SHN, and the DAT came from Todd Evans [1]
- **gd1974-03-23.aud.connors.hughey.gems.78599.flac16**: taped by DAT from collection of Todd Evans; transferred by DAT > TASCAM DA-20 > M-Audio Audiophile 192 > Soundforge 8.0 wav; source: Master Audience Cassette > Dat (or PCM?) [2]. Also: GEMS production from October 2006, edited in Wavelab 6.0 with BBE processing and Adobe Audition [2]
- **gd1974-03-23.aud.OBV-GEMS.83453.flac16**: transferred by Owen Brothers; source: AUD MC>(PCM?)>DAT>DA-20>M-Audio 192 (Shnid=78599) [3]. Also: Mastered by The Wizard using digital EQ to lift the midrange, with Diamond Cut DC6 editing [3]
- **gd1974-03-23.176294.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Louis Falanga's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 250 mic > Sony TC-110 (Maxell UD C120) [4]. Also: Charles Connor's Sony ECM 22p source supplies crowd and opening notes of U.S. Blues, Beat It On Down The Line, and Ramble On Rose [4]
- **gd74-03-23.sbd.clugston.1689.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [7]. Also: Main portions of the show were released on Dicks Picks 24 [10]
